subject: scorpion
pitch: A desert scorpion in a threatening pose, tail arched high over its back. Glossy amber armour with darker bands at every joint, big crab-like pincers held forward, eight thin legs, a segmented tail ending in a bulbous dark stinger, and a cluster of tiny black eyes on the head shield.
reasoning:
I'm planning out the scorpion model's scale and proportions, aiming for a total length around 0.25 meters with the body facing forward and standing on the ground plane, then setting up the builder structure to begin constructing it.

Now I'm figuring out the joint hierarchy — a pelvis root joint for the body, segmenting the abdomen going backward, and planning a tail chain that arches up and curls forward over the body to position the stinger near the top-front, working out the curve points for that arc.

I'm sweeping tapered geometry along the tail chain, varying the radius per segment to create a natural taper toward the tip.

For the stinger, I'm placing a small sphere at the chain's final joint, letting it inherit the rigid weighting from that point. I'm also planning dark banding along the tail joints, likely by varying color as a function of position along the sweep so the fill switches at specific thresholds.

Now I'm sketching the body geometry: a scaled sphere for the prosoma, and several stacked, scaled boxy segments for the mesosoma, with dark bands marking each segment boundary.

For the pedipalps and pincers, I'm planning chains of swept tubes for the arms, capsule shapes for the fingers, and a sphere-like palm, with the moveable finger set up as its own joint so the claw can open and close.

For the eight legs, I'm setting up a chain per side with catmull-spline paths running from hip through knee and ankle down to the foot, which naturally produces three joints per leg without needing extra configuration, and I'm placing them at staggered z-positions along the body so they read as paired legs along each flank.

I'm also working out the small details: explicitly setting each leg's parent to the body joint rather than relying on nearest-point inference, spreading the knees outward, and positioning tiny eye spheres and the scaled prosoma/mesosoma shapes relative to the body joint's coordinates.

Now I'm sketching the mesosoma segments as scaled spheres stepping back in z with shrinking size, plus thin dark band rings at each segment's front edge using rotated cylinders to create the disc-like banding effect.

Settling on local scale [0.033, 0.004, 0.024] for the dark bands, rendered as small dark-colored segments around the body.

For the tail, I'm planning a chain rooted at the mesosoma's rear, curving upward through several joints to a stinger tip positioned high and forward, like a scorpion's raised tail. I'll use a Catmull-Rom spline through the control points with evenly spaced segments (around 6 joints named automatically), and taper the tube radius from thicker at the base to thinner near the tip before widening again for the stinger bulb.

For coloring the tail, I'm writing a function that alternates between amber and dark bands based on fractional position along each segment, then adding a small dark sphere at the stinger tip and a thin spike geometry to represent the barb pointing forward.

Now I'm working out the pedipalps — building a chain for the left arm with control points curving outward and forward from the prosoma, parented to the body.

For the claw, I'm adding a joint at the chain tip to attach the pincer, then a sphere for the palm scaled flat and wide, colored amber. Next I need to add the gripping fingers off that palm joint.

Writing capsule finger geometry...

Mirroring the right claw by negating x, I set up a side-sign helper so left/right limbs share the same construction logic. For legs, I'm defining four hip positions per side with knee, ankle, and foot-tip points, then building catmull-rom chains per leg with naming conventions like "legL1" and auto-generated joint names.

I'm settling on tapered sweep radii (0.005 to 0.0025) for the legs using a darker amber tone, confirming the chain's radius array interpolates linearly across the joint range.

For the eyes, I'm placing six tiny black spheres (radius 0.0035) clustered on the front-top of the head shield, positioned symmetrically around the prosoma. I'm then working out the prosoma sphere placement and scale, and spacing out the five mesosoma segments with gradually decreasing scale along the z-axis, while noting that the tail chain's starting position overlaps awkwardly with the mesosoma segments and needs to be repositioned to the rear of the last segment.

Now I'm setting the tail path's starting point at the rear of the mesosoma, and defining the pedipalp arm chains starting from the front of the prosoma with a curved sequence of points leading out to a claw tip, keeping the joint naming and bone parenting consistent. I'm deciding to skip adding dark color bands to the arms for simplicity, since the catmull-rom knot spacing makes precise band placement unreliable, and instead keep the arms a uniform amber.

I'm picking out the material palette—amber, a darker brown for shadowed areas, a leg tone, and black for eyes—then adding a small dark sphere for the stinger bulb at the tail tip, sized and positioned using the chain's final joint, followed by a tapered spike piece for the stinger point itself using the same bone attachment.

I'm figuring out joint roles for the rig—spine for body segments, with tail, arm, and leg chains, plus a "digit" role for the claw fingers—before setting up the root body joint.

For the claws, I'm positioning the fixed and moving fingers of each pincer so their tips meet, mirroring left and right sides with a sign multiplier on x-coordinates. Now I'm placing the eye positions symmetrically on either side of the head.

I'll settle on roughly six eyes positioned in two rows, approximating their placement on the prosoma surface without being too precise about it, plus dark bands marking the prosoma-mesosoma joint and each segment.

For the sweeps, I'm using the chain-based sweep function with a radius that tapers along the tail and a color function sampled across the length, building the tail from six evenly spaced points along a smooth curve.

Now I'm structuring the actual module: setting up the imports, defining color constants for amber body, dark markings, leg color, and eye color, and starting the main builder function with the body joint positioned at the origin pointing forward.

Working through the mesosoma segments, I'm looping through five tapering body segments with alternating amber spheres and darker cylindrical bands marking the joints between them.

For the tail, I'm using a catmull-rom spline through curved control points to form the characteristic upward arch, creating a chain with six segments and sweeping a tapering radius along it with alternating dark/amber bands at the joints, then capping it with a dark stinger sphere and a sharp spike oriented along the tail's final tangent direction.

Now I'm building the eight legs in pairs across left and right sides, each as a catmull chain running from hip to ankle with named joints, swept with a thin tapering tube in the leg color, checking that the hip attachment points sit embedded within the body segments rather than floating outside them.

For the pedipalps, I'm chaining shoulder-elbow-wrist on each side up toward the front, sweeping tapering amber tubes, then adding a claw joint at the wrist tip with a bulbous palm sphere and two capsule fingers -- a fixed amber one and a moving dark-tipped one angled to meet it, mirrored for the opposite side.

Then I'm placing six small dark eye spheres in a cluster pattern on each side of the prosoma, mirrored across the x-axis.

I'm now double-checking overall proportions -- the tail arc length felt too long relative to the body, so I'm adjusting the spline points to shorten it to a more plausible curled length, and tapering its radius down so it reads as a thin tail rather than a thick one. I'm also verifying that the lowest points of the legs and tail stinger stay just above the ground plane so the model doesn't clip through the floor, and confirming the builder call signature and root joint setup are correct before finalizing the export.

I'm confirming the leg and arm chain joint-name arrays line up correctly with the number of spline segments, then wrapping up -- the final answer just needs the code output itself without much additional explanation.
